chunks: Humayd, from Ibn Sama'ah, from someone else, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who advanced dirhams for food, so what was due to him was released, and he sent the dirhams back to him, saying: 'Buy food and fulfill your right.' Do you see any problem with it? He said: 'If someone else were with him, that would be fulfilled.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on advancing money for food and the conditions for fulfilling the right in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the validity of *salaf* (advance payment for food) when the buyer receives the goods but the seller returns the cash with instructions to purchase food and settle the debt. The Imam specifies that the transaction remains sound provided there is another party present to ensure the fulfillment of the obligation, highlighting the Shia juristic emphasis on securing rights in deferred transactions. This reflects the broader principle of preventing *gharar* (uncertainty) in commercial exchanges by ensuring clear mechanisms for debt recovery.
